1: # Tiwas — Canonical Rules & Changelog
2: 
3: **Document Version:** v1.3  
4: **Document Status:** Canonical Source of Truth  
5: **Document Role:** Authoritative statement of the current Tiwas ruleset  
6: **Supersedes:** Canonical Rules & Changelog v1.2 and previous standalone Core Rules and locked subsystem documents for any material incorporated here  
7: **Historical material:** Preserved in compressed changelog form  
8: **Rule status vocabulary:** `Canonical / Locked`, `Reserved`, `Historical / Superseded`
9: 
10: ---
11: 
12: ## 0. Authority and Governance
13: 
14: This document is the authoritative source for Tiwas mechanics that have been formally locked.
15: 
16: Future Tiwas documentation must not contradict this document without an explicit rules-governance decision.
17: 
18: A mechanic appearing here is **Canonical / Locked** unless explicitly identified as Reserved.
19: 
20: ### 0.1 Authority hierarchy
21: 
22: Within the consolidated Tiwas documentation:
23: 
24: 1. **Canonical Rules & Changelog** — current locked mechanics.
25: 2. **Proposals, WIP & Design Direction** — unresolved and experimental design material.
26: 3. **Implementation Roadmap & Project Governance** — implementation sequencing and project-management guidance.
27: 
28: The latter two documents cannot override this document.
29: 
30: ### 0.2 Locked does not mean permanently immutable
31: 
32: "Locked" means:
33: 
34: > The mechanic is part of the current Tiwas ruleset and must be treated as authoritative by downstream design and implementation.
35: 
36: A locked mechanic may be reopened only through normal Tiwas design governance, normally because new simulation evidence, playtesting, conversion work, or another substantive design finding demonstrates a problem.
37: 
38: A proposal, recommendation, implementation convenience, or LLM preference does not by itself reopen a locked rule.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: # 1. Tiwas Core Identity
43: 
44: Tiwas is a high-consequence percentile universal RPG in which:
45: 
46: - every meaningful attempt uses the common resolution engine;
47: - every test costs resources;
48: - failure generates mechanical growth;
49: - meaningful success changes the tactical or narrative state.
50: 
51: The system's locked design priorities are:
52: 
53: 1. **Granular physical simulation where the situation warrants it.**
54: 2. **Heroic resilience / low permanent character loss rate.**
55: 3. **Minimum resolution steps per exchange without sacrificing Priority 1.**
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: # 2. Core Dice and Resolution
60: 
61: ## 2.1 d100
62: 
63: A Tiwas d100 produces an integer from **1–100**.
64: 
65: Physical percentile dice displaying `00` represent **100**, never zero.
66: 
67: ## 2.2 Roll-under
68: 
69: A skill test succeeds when:
70: 
71: `Roll <= Skill`
72: 
73: unless the 100-Fumble rule applies.
74: 
75: ## 2.3 100-Fumble
76: 
77: A roll of **100 always fails**, regardless of Skill value.
78: 
79: A roll of 100 is also always treated as a qualifying Double.
80: 
81: Therefore no Skill value produces literal 100% test reliability.
82: 
83: ## 2.4 Doubles
84: 
85: The canonical Double values are:
86: 
87: `11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, 99, 100`
88: 
89: A Double produces its special Advanced Skill effect only when the roll is also a Failure.
90: 
91: The nine digit-doubles qualify when the Double exceeds the tested Skill.
92: 
93: 100 always qualifies because 100 is always a Failure.
94: 
95: ## 2.5 Rounding
96: 
97: All fractional calculations use floor rounding.
98: 
99: There are no general exceptions to this rule.
100: 
101: ---
102: 
103: # 3. The 24-Attribute Matrix
104: 
105: Characters possess 24 independently generated attributes.
106: 
107: Each attribute is generated as:
108: 
109: `1d100`
110: 
111: The attributes are divided into twelve Body attributes and twelve Mind attributes.
112: 
113: | Code | Animal | Category | Tier-1 Skill |
114: |---|---|---|---|
115: | bpp | Bear | Body / Power / Power | Might |
116: | bps | Tiger | Body / Power / Speed | Impact |
117: | bpe | Elephant | Body / Power / Endurance | Brawn |
118: | bpx | Dragon | Body / Power / Social | Presence |
119: | bsp | Hawk | Body / Speed / Power | Agility |
120: | bss | Rat | Body / Speed / Speed | Reflexes |
121: | bse | Horse | Body / Speed / Endurance | Quickness |
122: | bsx | Monkey | Body / Speed / Social | Grace |
123: | bep | Badger | Body / Endurance / Power | Toughness |
124: | bes | Wolf | Body / Endurance / Speed | Stamina |
125: | bee | Ox | Body / Endurance / Endurance | Vitality |
126: | bex | Dog | Body / Endurance / Social | Poise |
127: | mpp | Stag | Mind / Power / Power | Cunning |
128: | mps | Snake | Mind / Power / Speed | Wits |
129: | mpe | Rooster | Mind / Power / Endurance | Willpower |
130: | mpx | Fox | Mind / Power / Social | Glamour |
131: | msp | Bat | Mind / Speed / Power | Acuity |
132: | mss | Cat | Mind / Speed / Speed | Perception |
133: | mse | Rabbit | Mind / Speed / Endurance | Alacrity |
134: | msx | Otter | Mind / Speed / Social | Charm |
135: | mep | Crane | Mind / Endurance / Power | Focus |
136: | mes | Goat | Mind / Endurance / Speed | Discipline |
137: | mee | Owl | Mind / Endurance / Endurance | Resolve |
138: | mex | Pig | Mind / Endurance / Social | Composure |
139: 
140: An attribute belongs permanently to either Body or Mind.
141: 
142: ---
143: 
144: # 4. Derived Statistics
145: 
146: Derived statistics are live calculations.
147: 
148: Changing an attribute immediately changes every derived statistic and Skill Cap that depends upon it.
149: 
150: | Statistic | Formula |
151: |---|---|
152: | Health Points (HP) | Sum of all 12 Body attributes |
153: | Mental Points (MP) | Sum of all 12 Mind attributes |
154: | Physical Energy | bep + bes + bee |
155: | Speed | bsp + bss + bse |
156: | Energy Regen | bep + bes |
157: | MP Regen | mep + mes |
158: | Movement Speed | floor((bsp + bss) / 15) |
159: 
160: MP is simultaneously the Mind resource pool and the total derived from the twelve Mind attributes. This identity is intentional.
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: # 5. Skills
165: 
166: ## 5.1 Skill Tier
167: 
168: A Skill's Tier is the number of **distinct attributes** used in its Cap formula.
169: 
170: A Tier-1 Skill uses one attribute.
171: 
172: A Tier-T Skill uses T attributes.
173: 
174: No attribute may appear more than once within a Skill formula.
175: 
176: The theoretical maximum Tier is therefore 24.
177: 
178: ## 5.2 Skill Cap
179: 
180: `Cap = floor((A1 + A2 + ... + AT) / T)`
181: 
182: The Cap is the floored average of the underlying attributes.
183: 
184: Increasing Tier does not inherently increase expected Cap; it averages additional attributes and reduces variance.
185: 
186: ## 5.3 Starting Skill
187: 
188: A normal Skill begins at:
189: 
190: `Starting Value = floor(Cap / 2)`
191: 
192: A Skill may therefore legitimately begin at 0.
193: 
194: ---
195: 
196: # 6. Canonical Test Transaction
197: 
198: Every Skill test follows this order:
199: 
200: 1. Roll 1d100.
201: 2. Determine the Skill's resource domain.
202: 3. Determine Success or Failure.
203: 4. Pay Cost equal to the natural roll.
204: 5. Apply Overflow if the resource pool cannot pay the full cost.
205: 6. Resolve Failure XP.
206: 7. Resolve qualifying failed Double / Advanced Skill effects.
207: 8. Recover the appropriate resource.
208: 9. End the test.
209: 
210: No Universal Play subsystem may replace this transaction with an alternative resolution engine.
211: 
212: ---
213: 
214: # 7. Resource Cost and Overflow
215: 
216: Every test costs the exact number rolled.
217: 
218: ### Body Skill
219: 
220: Cost is paid from Physical Energy.
221: 
222: ### Mind Skill
223: 
224: Cost is paid from MP.
225: 
226: If the available resource is insufficient:
227: 
228: `Overflow = Cost - Remaining Resource`
229: 
230: The resource pool falls to zero and the Overflow becomes direct HP damage.
231: 
232: Overflow does not create a second resource pool.
233: 
234: ---
235: 
236: # 8. Recovery
237: 
238: Recovery occurs **after every test** and is always the final stage.
239: 
240: The recovered amount is:
241: 
242: `floor(Regen / 2)`
243: 
244: Recovery applies to the resource pool just spent and is clamped at that pool's maximum.
245: 
246: Recovery occurs regardless of:
247: 
248: - success;
249: - failure;
250: - Overflow;
251: - failed Double;
252: - Advanced Skill creation.
253: 
254: A full Rest action remains Reserved and is not defined by the Core.
255: 
256: ---
257: 
258: # 9. Failure XP
259: 
260: Failure XP is:
261: 
262: `max(0, Roll - Skill)`
263: 
264: The clamp prevents negative XP when the 100-Fumble forces a failure against Skill 100 or higher.
265: 
266: ---
267: 
268: # 10. Skill Roll Pool
269: 
270: Failure XP first enters a temporary Skill Roll Pool.
271: 
272: The pool exists only for the current failed test.
273: 
274: It does not persist between tests.
275: 
276: Within the failed test:
277: 
278: ```text
279: while Pool >= Current Skill
280: and Current Skill < Cap:
281: 
282:     Pool -= Current Skill
283:     Skill += 1
284: ```
285: 
286: The process stops when:
287: 
288: - the remaining pool cannot afford another increase; or
289: - the Skill reaches its Cap.
290: 
291: Any remaining pool becomes General XP.
292: 
293: ## 10.1 Skill at 0
294: 
295: If a Skill is 0, the cost of increasing it to 1 is zero.
296: 
297: Therefore a failed test with nonzero Failure XP raises a Skill-0 to at least 1 immediately.
298: 
299: This is intentional.
300: 
301: ---
302: 
303: # 11. General XP
304: 
305: General XP receives:
306: 
307: - Skill Roll Pool remainder;
308: - GM/quest/adventure awards.
309: 
310: General XP may increase:
311: 
312: - Attributes;
313: - Skills.
314: 
315: The cost of increasing a value by 1 is its current value.
316: 
317: General XP must cover the entire cost of an increase.
318: 
319: Partial advancement is not permitted.
320: 
321: ## 11.1 Above-Cap advancement
322: 
323: General XP may raise a Skill above its current Cap.
324: 
325: Skill Roll Pool advancement may not.
326: 
327: ## 11.2 Advancement ceiling
328: 
329: The initial 1–100 range applies to attribute generation.
330: 
331: Advancement has no fixed upper bound.
332: 
333: Skills above 100 remain subject to the mandatory 100-Fumble.
334: 
335: ---
336: 
337: # 12. Advanced Skills
338: 
339: A qualifying failed Double immediately creates an Advanced Skill.
340: 
341: ## 12.1 Creation
342: 
343: 1. New Skill Tier = failed Skill Tier + 1.
344: 2. Add one attribute not already present in the failed Skill formula.
345: 3. Recalculate the new Cap from the complete attribute set.
346: 4. Choose either:
347:    - starting value 1; or
348:    - roll 1d100 and use `min(Roll, New Cap)`.
349: 
350: ## 12.2 Duplicate restrictions
351: 
352: An attribute cannot appear twice within a single Skill formula.
353: 
354: The same Advanced Skill — defined by the same base Skill and added attribute — cannot be created twice.
355: 
356: ## 12.3 Resource domain
357: 
358: An Advanced Skill retains the resource domain of its original Tier-1 lineage.
359: 
360: A Body-rooted lineage remains Physical Energy based even if later attributes include Mind attributes.
361: 
362: A Mind-rooted lineage remains MP based even if later attributes include Body attributes.
363: 
364: ## 12.4 Advancement depth
365: 
366: Advanced Skills may themselves generate further Advanced Skills.
367: 
368: There is no arbitrary Tier ceiling beyond the natural 24-attribute limit.
369: 
370: ---
371: 
372: # 13. Universal Opposed Contest — S-1
373: 
374: **Status: Canonical / Locked**
375: 
376: S-1 is the universal opposed-contest primitive.
377: 
378: Each participant performs an ordinary Core Test independently.
379: 
380: The contest layer does not alter the underlying test.
381: 
382: ## 13.1 Outcome matrix
383: 
384: | Participant A | Participant B | Result |
385: |---|---|---|
386: | Success | Failure | A wins |
387: | Failure | Success | B wins |
388: | Success | Success | Compare Quality |
389: | Failure | Failure | Repeat contest |
390: 
391: Each participant pays their own natural roll cost and resolves their own Failure XP, Double eligibility and Recovery.
392: 
393: ## 13.2 Quality measures
394: 
395: The Quality measure is selected by contest type.
396: 
397: | Mode | Formula | Primary identity |
398: |---|---|---|
399: | Margin | `Skill - Roll` | Efficiency / precision |
400: | Blackjack | `Roll` | Commitment / force |
401: | Hybrid Committed | `Roll + max(0, Skill - 99)` | Commitment with continued high-Skill scaling |
402: 
403: Quality only compares already-rolled successful tests.
404: 
405: It never modifies:
406: 
407: - the historical roll;
408: - Cost;
409: - Failure XP;
410: - Double eligibility;
411: - Recovery.
412: 
413: ## 13.3 Quality selection
414: 
415: Current guidance:
416: 
417: | Situation | Default |
418: |---|---|
419: | Precision / efficiency | Margin |
420: | Force / commitment | Blackjack |
421: | Mixed / uncertain | Hybrid |
422: 
423: Blackjack and Hybrid's distinctive identity becomes meaningful primarily once relevant Skills are sufficiently high. At low Skill, the success/failure gate dominates.
424: 
425: The GM may override situational guidance where the fiction demands another Quality measure.
426: 
427: ## 13.4 Failure/Failure
428: 
429: Both participants repeat the contest.
430: 
431: Both tests have already incurred all normal Core consequences before the repeat occurs.
432: 
433: ## 13.5 Exact Quality tie
434: 
435: An exact Quality tie causes the contest to repeat.
436: 
437: The repeat is a fresh contest round.
438: 
439: ## 13.6 S-1 validation
440: 
441: S-1 has been validated through simulation across Skill 10–250 and Skill gaps up to 151.
442: 
443: The empirical validation and designer rulings are retained as historical design evidence rather than treated as mathematical rules themselves.
444: 
445: ---
446: 
447: # 14. S-2 — Tier-1 Location Index Provider
448: 
449: **Status: Canonical / Locked — limited S-2 decision**
450: 
451: This section locks only the Tier-1 Location Index provider. It does not complete the broader hit-location subsystem.
452: 
453: ## 14.1 Zero-Step
454: 
455: When a rule calls for a Tier-1 Location Index, use **Zero-Step**.
456: 
457: Zero-Step derives the Location Index by exchanging the tens and units digits of the attacker's natural d100 roll. Interpret `00` as `100` under the normal d100 rule after the exchange.
458: 
459: Examples:
460: 
461: | Natural d100 roll | Zero-Step Location Index |
462: |---:|---:|
463: | 37 | 73 |
464: | 10 | 1 |
465: | 1 | 10 |
466: | 100 (`00`) | 100 (`00`) |
467: 
468: For physical percentile dice, exchange the displayed tens and units digits. For another rolling method, express the natural roll as its two percentile digits before exchanging them.
469: 
470: ## 14.2 Determinism and player choice
471: 
472: Zero-Step is deterministic. The attacker does not choose between the natural roll and the transformed result.
473: 
474: The natural roll remains authoritative for every Core Test consequence, including outcome, Cost, Overflow, Failure XP, failed-Double eligibility, Advanced Skill effects and Recovery. The transformed result is used only as the Tier-1 Location Index.
475: 
476: ## 14.3 Scope retained for later S-2 work
477: 
478: The following are not established by this ruling:
479: 
480: - whether and when a scene uses Tier 0, Tier 1 or Tier 2 location granularity;
481: - Tier-0 and Tier-2 procedures;
482: - anatomical mapping from a Location Index to a zone;
483: - wound, armour, defence and Outcome Effect interaction;
484: - whether any later rule may select, modify or consume a Location Index.
485: 
486: These matters remain non-canonical until separately resolved through governance.
487: 
488: ## 14.4 Future optional-rule observations
489: 
490: Playtest participants suggested choosing between the natural and swapped values. That suggestion is not part of the basic rule and creates no player choice in current Tiwas.
491: 
492: The designer may later consider, in an optional-rule appendix only:
493: 
494: - an attacker choice granted by an explicit special ability; and
495: - a defender choice.
496: 
497: Neither observation is a current rule, a permission, or a design commitment.
498: 
499: ## 14.5 E9 human usability playtest record
500: 
501: **Evidence class: Empirical finding — passed for the tested physical two-d10 method only.**
502: 
503: The E9 usability playtest used two physical d10s and 50 participants: 25 participants new to RPGs and 25 RPG players new to Tiwas. Participants reported no difficulty rolling the dice or exchanging the digits for hit location, and feedback was positive.
504: 
505: This evidence supports usability of Zero-Step for that tested physical two-d10 method. Other input methods, including a single d100, a digital roller, and a verbally announced result, were not tested and are not covered by this finding. E9 supports the designer ruling but does not resolve the remaining S-2 architecture.
506: 
507: ## 14.6 Comparative derivation-cost residual
508: 
509: Separate from E9, the completed comparative analysis found that Units-Digit requires 0–1 additional derivation operations across the examined rolling modes, while Zero-Step requires 1–2. This is a comparative structural observation about derivation steps, not a human-usability finding and not an additional E9 status.
510: 
511: The completed physical two-d10 playtest establishes usability only for its tested method. Any relative cost or usability conclusion for other input methods remains outside that playtest's evidence.
512: 
513: ---
514: 
515: # 15. Reserved Systems
516: 
517: The following remain outside the locked Core unless separately incorporated into this document through formal governance:
518: 
519: - hit-location rules, except the Tier-1 Zero-Step Location Index provider in Section 14;
520: - wound activation/severity;
521: - Outcome Effects;
522: - armor;
523: - active/passive defense;
524: - incapacitation;
525: - death;
526: - healing;
527: - Rest;
528: - equipment;
529: - encumbrance;
530: - conditions;
531: - environmental hazards;
532: - difficulty grades;
533: - task/stakes adjudication;
534: - Extended Tests;
535: - NPC construction;
536: - magic/special-ability implementation;
537: - GM procedure;
538: - campaign procedures;
539: - setting-specific content.
540: 
541: Where a separate Universal Play subsystem has already been locked, such as S-1, its current rules supersede the older "Reserved" classification.
542: 
543: ---
544: 
545: # 16. Core Architectural Invariants
546: 
547: Every future Tiwas subsystem must preserve:
548: 
549: 1. d100 produces 1–100.
550: 2. 100 always fails.
551: 3. 100 is a qualifying failed Double.
552: 4. All fractions floor.
553: 5. Success is roll-under.
554: 6. Cost equals the natural roll.
555: 7. Overflow becomes HP damage.
556: 8. Failure XP uses `max(0, Roll - Skill)`.
557: 9. Skill Roll Pool is temporary.
558: 10. Skill Roll Pool advancement cannot exceed Cap.
559: 11. General XP can exceed Cap.
560: 12. Failed Doubles can create Advanced Skills.
561: 13. Advanced Skill Caps are recalculated from the full attribute set.
562: 14. Advanced Skill resource domain follows lineage.
563: 15. Derived statistics are live.
564: 16. Recovery occurs last.
565: 17. No Universal Play subsystem may introduce a competing primary resource or progression economy.
566: 18. Universal Play modules must build on the Core Test Transaction rather than replace it.
567: 
568: ---
569: 
570: # 17. Changelog
571: 
572: ## Core v1 → Core v2
573: 
574: The following ambiguities were formally closed in Core Rules v2:
575: 
576: 1. d100 range and interpretation of `00`.
577: 2. Complete Double list.
578: 3. Tier ≥2 Cap calculation.
579: 4. Advanced Skill Cap recomputation.
580: 5. Skill Roll Pool persistence.
581: 6. Cascading advancement.
582: 7. Skill-0 advancement.
583: 8. Fractional recovery rounding.
584: 9. Recovery timing and clamping.
585: 10. Advanced Skill creation timing.
586: 11. Duplicate attributes.
587: 12. Duplicate Advanced Skills.
588: 13. Mixed-domain Advanced Skill resource type.
589: 14. Maximum Tier.
590: 15. Removal of a separate Cap-purchase mechanic.
591: 16. General XP above Cap.
592: 17. Advancement upper bound.
593: 18. Guaranteed success at high Skill.
594: 19. Status of undeveloped subsystems.
595: 
596: ## S-1 v1 → v1.1
597: 
598: The locked S-1 closure pass:
599: 
600: 1. Clarified wording around Skills above 99.
601: 2. Extended validation of the cost-asymmetry identity through Skill 250.
602: 3. Added the canonical quick-reference procedure.
603: 4. Locked exact Quality ties as Repeat.
604: 5. Locked Failure/Failure as Repeat.
605: 6. Confirmed the Skill-gating caveat for Blackjack and Hybrid.
606: 7. Kept the S-1D stance experiment explicitly outside canonical S-1.
607: 
608: ## S-2 v1.1 → v1.2
609: 
610: 1. Locked Zero-Step as the Tier-1 Location Index provider.
611: 2. Locked Zero-Step as deterministic: players do not choose between the natural and transformed results.
612: 3. Confirmed that Zero-Step is a read-only post-process and does not alter any Core Test consequence.
613: 4. Recorded the E9 human usability playtest as supporting empirical evidence.
614: 5. Retained the broader S-2 architecture, including tier policy and anatomical mapping, as unresolved.
615: 6. Recorded attacker special-ability choice and defender choice only as future optional-rule observations.
616: 
617: ## S-2 documentation reconciliation v1.3
618: 
619: 1. Clarified that the completed E9 playtest passes only for the tested physical two-d10 method.
620: 2. Explicitly recorded that single-d100, digital, and verbally announced input methods remain untested.
621: 3. Separated the comparative derivation-cost residual from E9 so that structural comparison and human evidence do not receive conflicting labels.
622: 4. Preserved Zero-Step as the deterministic canonical Tier-1 provider; preserved the broader S-2 architecture as unresolved.
623: 
624: ## Consolidation change
625: 
626: The former Core statement that opposed tests were Reserved is now historical because S-1 formally closes that subsystem.
627: 
628: The original Tiwas v1 documentation remains historical and superseded by Core Rules v2.
629: 

(End of file - total 629 lines)

# Tiwas — Canonical Rules & Changelog

**Document Version:** v1.3  
**Document Status:** Canonical Source of Truth  
**Document Role:** Authoritative statement of the current Tiwas ruleset

**Historical material:** Preserved in compressed changelog form  
**Rule status vocabulary:** `Canonical / Locked`, `Reserved`, `Historical / Superseded`

---

## 0. Authority and Governance

This document is the authoritative source for Tiwas mechanics that have been formally locked.

Future Tiwas documentation must not contradict this document without an explicit rules-governance decision.

A mechanic appearing here is **Canonical / Locked** unless explicitly identified as Reserved.

### 0.1 Authority hierarchy

Within the consolidated Tiwas documentation:

1. **Canonical Rules & Changelog** — current locked mechanics.
2. **Proposals, WIP & Design Direction** — unresolved and experimental design material.
3. **Implementation Roadmap & Project Governance** — implementation sequencing and project-management guidance.

The latter two documents cannot override this document.

### 0.2 Locked does not mean permanently immutable

"Locked" means:

> The mechanic is part of the current Tiwas ruleset and must be treated as authoritative by downstream design and implementation.

A locked mechanic may be reopened only through normal Tiwas design governance, normally because new simulation evidence, playtesting, conversion work, or another substantive design finding demonstrates a problem.

A proposal, recommendation, implementation convenience, or LLM preference does not by itself reopen a locked rule.

---

# 1. Tiwas Core Identity

Tiwas is a high-consequence percentile universal RPG in which:

- every meaningful attempt uses the common resolution engine;
- every test costs resources;
- failure generates mechanical growth;
- meaningful success changes the tactical or narrative state.

The system's locked design priorities are:

1. **Granular physical simulation where the situation warrants it.**
2. **Heroic resilience / low permanent character loss rate.**
3. **Minimum resolution steps per exchange without sacrificing Priority 1.**

---

# 2. Core Dice and Resolution

## 2.1 d100

A Tiwas d100 produces an integer from **1–100**.

Physical percentile dice displaying `00` represent **100**, never zero.

## 2.2 Roll-under

A skill test succeeds when:

`Roll <= Skill`

unless the 100-Fumble rule applies.

## 2.3 100-Fumble

A roll of **100 always fails**, regardless of Skill value.

A roll of 100 is also always treated as a qualifying Double.

Therefore no Skill value produces literal 100% test reliability.

## 2.4 Doubles

The canonical Double values are:

`11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, 99, 100`

A Double produces its special Advanced Skill effect only when the roll is also a Failure.

The nine digit-doubles qualify when the Double exceeds the tested Skill.

100 always qualifies because 100 is always a Failure.

## 2.5 Rounding

All fractional calculations use floor rounding.

There are no general exceptions to this rule.

---

# 3. The 24-Attribute Matrix

Characters possess 24 independently generated attributes.

Each attribute is generated as:

`1d100`

The attributes are divided into twelve Body attributes and twelve Mind attributes.

| Code | Animal | Category | Tier-1 Skill |
|---|---|---|---|
| bpp | Bear | Body / Power / Power | Might |
| bps | Tiger | Body / Power / Speed | Impact |
| bpe | Elephant | Body / Power / Endurance | Brawn |
| bpx | Dragon | Body / Power / Social | Presence |
| bsp | Hawk | Body / Speed / Power | Agility |
| bss | Rat | Body / Speed / Speed | Reflexes |
| bse | Horse | Body / Speed / Endurance | Quickness |
| bsx | Monkey | Body / Speed / Social | Grace |
| bep | Badger | Body / Endurance / Power | Toughness |
| bes | Wolf | Body / Endurance / Speed | Stamina |
| bee | Ox | Body / Endurance / Endurance | Vitality |
| bex | Dog | Body / Endurance / Social | Poise |
| mpp | Stag | Mind / Power / Power | Cunning |
| mps | Snake | Mind / Power / Speed | Wits |
| mpe | Rooster | Mind / Power / Endurance | Willpower |
| mpx | Fox | Mind / Power / Social | Glamour |
| msp | Bat | Mind / Speed / Power | Acuity |
| mss | Cat | Mind / Speed / Speed | Perception |
| mse | Rabbit | Mind / Speed / Endurance | Alacrity |
| msx | Otter | Mind / Speed / Social | Charm |
| mep | Crane | Mind / Endurance / Power | Focus |
| mes | Goat | Mind / Endurance / Speed | Discipline |
| mee | Owl | Mind / Endurance / Endurance | Resolve |
| mex | Pig | Mind / Endurance / Social | Composure |

An attribute belongs permanently to either Body or Mind.

---

# 4. Derived Statistics

Derived statistics are live calculations.

Changing an attribute immediately changes every derived statistic and Skill Cap that depends upon it.

| Statistic | Formula |
|---|---|
| Health Points (HP) | Sum of all 12 Body attributes |
| Mental Points (MP) | Sum of all 12 Mind attributes |
| Physical Energy | bep + bes + bee |
| Speed | bsp + bss + bse |
| Energy Regen | bep + bes |
| MP Regen | mep + mes |
| Movement Speed | floor((bsp + bss) / 15) |

MP is simultaneously the Mind resource pool and the total derived from the twelve Mind attributes. This identity is intentional.

---

# 5. Skills

## 5.1 Skill Tier

A Skill's Tier is the number of **distinct attributes** used in its Cap formula.

A Tier-1 Skill uses one attribute.

A Tier-T Skill uses T attributes.

No attribute may appear more than once within a Skill formula.

The theoretical maximum Tier is therefore 24.

## 5.2 Skill Cap

`Cap = floor((A1 + A2 + ... + AT) / T)`

The Cap is the floored average of the underlying attributes.

Increasing Tier does not inherently increase expected Cap; it averages additional attributes and reduces variance.

## 5.3 Starting Skill

A normal Skill begins at:

`Starting Value = floor(Cap / 2)`

A Skill may therefore legitimately begin at 0.

---

# 6. Canonical Test Transaction

Every Skill test follows this order:

1. Roll 1d100.
2. Determine the Skill's resource domain.
3. Determine Success or Failure.
4. Pay Cost equal to the natural roll.
5. Apply Overflow if the resource pool cannot pay the full cost.
6. Resolve Failure XP.
7. Resolve qualifying failed Double / Advanced Skill effects.
8. Recover the appropriate resource.
9. End the test.

No Universal Play subsystem may replace this transaction with an alternative resolution engine.

---

# 7. Resource Cost and Overflow

Every test costs the exact number rolled.

### Body Skill

Cost is paid from Physical Energy.

### Mind Skill

Cost is paid from MP.

If the available resource is insufficient:

`Overflow = Cost - Remaining Resource`

The resource pool falls to zero and the Overflow becomes direct HP damage.

Overflow does not create a second resource pool.

---

# 8. Recovery

Recovery occurs **after every test** and is always the final stage.

The recovered amount is:

`floor(Regen / 2)`

Recovery applies to the resource pool just spent and is clamped at that pool's maximum.

Recovery occurs regardless of:

- success;
- failure;
- Overflow;
- failed Double;
- Advanced Skill creation.

A full Rest action remains Reserved and is not defined by the Core.

---

# 9. Failure XP

Failure XP is:

`max(0, Roll - Skill)`

The clamp prevents negative XP when the 100-Fumble forces a failure against Skill 100 or higher.

---

# 10. Skill Roll Pool

Failure XP first enters a temporary Skill Roll Pool.

The pool exists only for the current failed test.

It does not persist between tests.

Within the failed test:

```text
while Pool >= Current Skill
and Current Skill < Cap:

    Pool -= Current Skill
    Skill += 1
```

The process stops when:

- the remaining pool cannot afford another increase; or
- the Skill reaches its Cap.

Any remaining pool becomes General XP.

## 10.1 Skill at 0

If a Skill is 0, the cost of increasing it to 1 is zero.

Therefore a failed test with nonzero Failure XP raises a Skill-0 to at least 1 immediately.

This is intentional.

---

# 11. General XP

General XP receives:

- Skill Roll Pool remainder;
- GM/quest/adventure awards.

General XP may increase:

- Attributes;
- Skills.

The cost of increasing a value by 1 is its current value.

General XP must cover the entire cost of an increase.

Partial advancement is not permitted.

## 11.1 Above-Cap advancement

General XP may raise a Skill above its current Cap.

Skill Roll Pool advancement may not.

## 11.2 Advancement ceiling

The initial 1–100 range applies to attribute generation.

Advancement has no fixed upper bound.

Skills above 100 remain subject to the mandatory 100-Fumble.

---

# 12. Advanced Skills

A qualifying failed Double immediately creates an Advanced Skill.

## 12.1 Creation

1. New Skill Tier = failed Skill Tier + 1.
2. Add one attribute not already present in the failed Skill formula.
3. Recalculate the new Cap from the complete attribute set.
4. Choose either:
   - starting value 1; or
   - roll 1d100 and use `min(Roll, New Cap)`.

## 12.2 Duplicate restrictions

An attribute cannot appear twice within a single Skill formula.

The same Advanced Skill — defined by the same base Skill and added attribute — cannot be created twice.

## 12.3 Resource domain

An Advanced Skill retains the resource domain of its original Tier-1 lineage.

A Body-rooted lineage remains Physical Energy based even if later attributes include Mind attributes.

A Mind-rooted lineage remains MP based even if later attributes include Body attributes.

## 12.4 Advancement depth

Advanced Skills may themselves generate further Advanced Skills.

There is no arbitrary Tier ceiling beyond the natural 24-attribute limit.

---

# 13. Universal Opposed Contest — S-1

**Status: Canonical / Locked**

S-1 is the universal opposed-contest primitive.

Each participant performs an ordinary Core Test independently.

The contest layer does not alter the underlying test.

## 13.1 Outcome matrix

| Participant A | Participant B | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Success | Failure | A wins |
| Failure | Success | B wins |
| Success | Success | Compare Quality |
| Failure | Failure | Repeat contest |

Each participant pays their own natural roll cost and resolves their own Failure XP, Double eligibility and Recovery.

## 13.2 Quality measures

The Quality measure is selected by contest type.

| Mode | Formula | Primary identity |
|---|---|---|
| Margin | `Skill - Roll` | Efficiency / precision |
| Blackjack | `Roll` | Commitment / force |
| Hybrid Committed | `Roll + max(0, Skill - 99)` | Commitment with continued high-Skill scaling |

Quality only compares already-rolled successful tests.

It never modifies:

- the historical roll;
- Cost;
- Failure XP;
- Double eligibility;
- Recovery.

## 13.3 Quality selection

Current guidance:

| Situation | Default |
|---|---|
| Precision / efficiency | Margin |
| Force / commitment | Blackjack |
| Mixed / uncertain | Hybrid |

Blackjack and Hybrid's distinctive identity becomes meaningful primarily once relevant Skills are sufficiently high. At low Skill, the success/failure gate dominates.

The GM may override situational guidance where the fiction demands another Quality measure.

## 13.4 Failure/Failure

Both participants repeat the contest.

Both tests have already incurred all normal Core consequences before the repeat occurs.

## 13.5 Exact Quality tie

An exact Quality tie causes the contest to repeat.

The repeat is a fresh contest round.

## 13.6 S-1 validation

S-1 has been validated through simulation across Skill 10–250 and Skill gaps up to 151.

The empirical validation and designer rulings are retained as historical design evidence rather than treated as mathematical rules themselves.

---

# 14. S-2 — Tier-1 Location Index Provider

**Status: Canonical / Locked — limited S-2 decision**

This section locks only the Tier-1 Location Index provider. It does not complete the broader hit-location subsystem.

## 14.1 Zero-Step

When a rule calls for a Tier-1 Location Index, use **Zero-Step**.

Zero-Step derives the Location Index by exchanging the tens and units digits of the attacker's natural d100 roll. Interpret `00` as `100` under the normal d100 rule after the exchange.

Examples:

| Natural d100 roll | Zero-Step Location Index |
|---:|---:|
| 37 | 73 |
| 10 | 1 |
| 1 | 10 |
| 100 (`00`) | 100 (`00`) |

For physical percentile dice, exchange the displayed tens and units digits. For another rolling method, express the natural roll as its two percentile digits before exchanging them.

## 14.2 Determinism and player choice

Zero-Step is deterministic. The attacker does not choose between the natural roll and the transformed result.

The natural roll remains authoritative for every Core Test consequence, including outcome, Cost, Overflow, Failure XP, failed-Double eligibility, Advanced Skill effects and Recovery. The transformed result is used only as the Tier-1 Location Index.

## 14.3 Scope retained for later S-2 work

The following are not established by this ruling:

- whether and when a scene uses Tier 0, Tier 1 or Tier 2 location granularity;
- Tier-0 and Tier-2 procedures;
- anatomical mapping from a Location Index to a zone;
- wound, armour, defence and Outcome Effect interaction;
- whether any later rule may select, modify or consume a Location Index.

These matters remain non-canonical until separately resolved through governance.

## 14.4 Future optional-rule observations

Playtest participants suggested choosing between the natural and swapped values. That suggestion is not part of the basic rule and creates no player choice in current Tiwas.

The designer may later consider, in an optional-rule appendix only:

- an attacker choice granted by an explicit special ability; and
- a defender choice.

Neither observation is a current rule, a permission, or a design commitment.

## 14.5 E9 human usability playtest record

**Evidence class: Empirical finding — passed for the tested physical two-d10 method only.**

The E9 usability playtest used two physical d10s and 50 participants: 25 participants new to RPGs and 25 RPG players new to Tiwas. Participants reported no difficulty rolling the dice or exchanging the digits for hit location, and feedback was positive.

This evidence supports usability of Zero-Step for that tested physical two-d10 method. Other input methods, including a single d100, a digital roller, and a verbally announced result, were not tested and are not covered by this finding. E9 supports the designer ruling but does not resolve the remaining S-2 architecture.

## 14.6 Comparative derivation-cost residual

Separate from E9, the completed comparative analysis found that Units-Digit requires 0–1 additional derivation operations across the examined rolling modes, while Zero-Step requires 1–2. This is a comparative structural observation about derivation steps, not a human-usability finding and not an additional E9 status.

The completed physical two-d10 playtest establishes usability only for its tested method. Any relative cost or usability conclusion for other input methods remains outside that playtest's evidence.

---

# 15. Reserved Systems

The following remain outside the locked Core unless separately incorporated into this document through formal governance:

- hit-location rules, except the Tier-1 Zero-Step Location Index provider in Section 14;
- wound activation/severity;
- Outcome Effects;
- armor;
- active/passive defense;
- incapacitation;
- death;
- healing;
- Rest;
- equipment;
- encumbrance;
- conditions;
- environmental hazards;
- difficulty grades;
- task/stakes adjudication;
- Extended Tests;
- NPC construction;
- magic/special-ability implementation;
- GM procedure;
- campaign procedures;
- setting-specific content.

Where a separate Universal Play subsystem has already been locked, such as S-1, its current rules supersede the older "Reserved" classification.

---

# 16. Core Architectural Invariants

Every future Tiwas subsystem must preserve:

1. d100 produces 1–100.
2. 100 always fails.
3. 100 is a qualifying failed Double.
4. All fractions floor.
5. Success is roll-under.
6. Cost equals the natural roll.
7. Overflow becomes HP damage.
8. Failure XP uses `max(0, Roll - Skill)`.
9. Skill Roll Pool is temporary.
10. Skill Roll Pool advancement cannot exceed Cap.
11. General XP can exceed Cap.
12. Failed Doubles can create Advanced Skills.
13. Advanced Skill Caps are recalculated from the full attribute set.
14. Advanced Skill resource domain follows lineage.
15. Derived statistics are live.
16. Recovery occurs last.
17. No Universal Play subsystem may introduce a competing primary resource or progression economy.
18. Universal Play modules must build on the Core Test Transaction rather than replace it.

---

# 17. Changelog

## Core v1 → Core v2

The following ambiguities were formally closed in Core Rules v2:

1. d100 range and interpretation of `00`.
2. Complete Double list.
3. Tier ≥2 Cap calculation.
4. Advanced Skill Cap recomputation.
5. Skill Roll Pool persistence.
6. Cascading advancement.
7. Skill-0 advancement.
8. Fractional recovery rounding.
9. Recovery timing and clamping.
10. Advanced Skill creation timing.
11. Duplicate attributes.
12. Duplicate Advanced Skills.
13. Mixed-domain Advanced Skill resource type.
14. Maximum Tier.
15. Removal of a separate Cap-purchase mechanic.

17. Advancement upper bound.
18. Guaranteed success at high Skill.
19. Status of undeveloped subsystems.

## S-1 v1 → v1.1

The locked S-1 closure pass:

1. Clarified wording around Skills above 99.
2. Extended validation of the cost-asymmetry identity through Skill 250.
3. Added the canonical quick-reference procedure.
4. Locked exact Quality ties as Repeat.
5. Locked Failure/Failure as Repeat.
6. Confirmed the Skill-gating caveat for Blackjack and Hybrid.
7. Kept the S-1D stance experiment explicitly outside canonical S-1.

## S-2 v1.1 → v1.2

1. Locked Zero-Step as the Tier-1 Location Index provider.
2. Locked Zero-Step as deterministic: players do not choose between the natural and transformed results.
3. Confirmed that Zero-Step is a read-only post-process and does not alter any Core Test consequence.
4. Recorded the E9 human usability playtest as supporting empirical evidence.
5. Retained the broader S-2 architecture, including tier policy and anatomical mapping, as unresolved.
6. Recorded attacker special-ability choice and defender choice only as future optional-rule observations.

## S-2 documentation reconciliation v1.3

2. Explicitly recorded that single-d100, digital, and verbally announced input methods remain untested.
3. Separated the comparative derivation-cost residual from E9 so that structural comparison and human evidence do not receive conflicting labels.
4. Preserved Zero-Step as the deterministic canonical Tier-1 provider; preserved the broader S-2 architecture as unresolved.

## Consolidation change

The former Core statement that opposed tests were Reserved is now historical because S-1 formally closes that subsystem.

The original Tiwas v1 documentation remains historical and superseded by Core Rules v2.

32: # 0. Purpose

Future subsystem design work should treat this as an open fork, not a settled assumption in either direction.
287: - **Non-attack Location Index source — RESOLVED AS A DEFERRAL (v1.4.3).** No longer an open implementation question in the "undecided mechanism" sense; the mechanism question (H0 and riders) is on record but inactive, and the category is categorically off until S-4/S-7/S-8 reopens it.
288: 
289: The broader tier policy, anatomical mapping, and downstream interaction remain open and require their own design and validation gates. Do not treat the completed Tier-1 provider decision, the promoted attack-side invocation policy (§14.7), or the non-attack ruling as closure of S-2 as a whole.
290: 
291: ---
292: 
293: # 10. Phase 3 — S-3 Outcome Effects and S-3/S-4 Interface Prototyping
294: 
295: **S-3 status: Open. S-4 status: Open.**
296: 
297: Implement the structural Effect interface first. Candidate Effects include Injury; Condition; Disarm / Break Hold; Movement / Position; Tempo; Guard Break; Bleed / Drain; Retreat / Yield; Equipment Damage; and Location selection.
298: 
299: S-3 work may prototype how an Effect passes harm or state information to a prospective S-4 Wound Engine. Such a prototype is an architectural exercise, not a lock on S-4. In particular, it must not silently establish wound severity thresholds, activation triggers, disability effects, or death checks.
300: 
301: The prospective two-track harm interface is:
302: 
303: ```text
304: Track A                         Track B
305: PE / MP                         Location
306:    ↓                               ↓
307: Overflow                        Wound
308:    ↓                               ↓
309: Global HP                       Condition / Disability / Death Check
310: ```
311: 
312: Acceptance criteria:
313: 
314: - Effects create real state changes.
315: - Effects do not alter historical rolls.
316: - Empty PE/MP is not automatic defeat.
317: - Overflow remains HP damage.
318: - HP = 0 is not automatically death.
319: - Wounds are not a second HP pool.
320: 
321: Simulation gate: measure Effect frequency, exchange length, resource expenditure, wound frequency, severe injury, and state-change density. Do not lock numerical thresholds without required evidence and a designer ruling.
322: 
323: ---
324: 
325: # 11. Phase 4 — Armor and Defense
326: 
327: ## 11.1 Armor
328: 
329: Implement Armor Traits and Tags, Bypass and Sunder interfaces, location interaction, and equipment damage. Compare candidates for bookkeeping, tactical value, simulation fidelity, and resolution steps.
330: 
331: ## 11.2 Defense
332: 
333: Implement passive and active defense interfaces, defense as a normal contest participant, resource interaction, and timing. Compare candidates for PE/MP drain, number of rolls, survivability, tactical decision density, and resolution steps.
334: 
335: No candidate should be promoted to Canonical merely because it is convenient to implement.
336: 
337: ---
338: 
339: # 12. Phase 5 — Incapacitation and Death
340: 
341: Implement HP-zero state, incapacitation, stabilization, survival, permanent injury, death, and recovery from incapacitation.
342: 
343: > **Simulation target:** Preserve heroic resilience while retaining meaningful physical consequences.
344: 
345: The permanent character-loss rate must be measured. No proposed death threshold becomes Canonical until the decision gate is passed.
346: 
347: **Note (v1.4.3):** this phase is one of the two subsystems flagged as a reopening trigger for the S-2 non-attack Location Index deferral (Proposals/WIP §2.5A). When incapacitation/death design work reaches a stage where hazard severity plausibly needs location-level resolution, that should be raised as an explicit reopening of the S-2 non-attack question, not silently assumed.
348: 
349: ---
350: 
351: # 13. Phase 6 — Difficulty and Task Adjudication
352: 
353: Implement difficulty grades, Skill-side modification, Skill selection, and opposed/unopposed selection. Verify interaction with Cost, Failure XP, 100-Fumble, Doubles, and Advanced Skills. Difficulty must not alter the natural die face.
354: 
355: **Note (v1.4.3, updated 2026-09-01):** the Stakes Gate is **REJECTED (DEC-051)** — no pre-Core-Test "skip the roll" filter exists for stakes-based reasons. Stakes Gate is struck from Phase 6 scope. The S-2 non-attack Location Index deferral reopening pathway previously flagged on the Stakes Gate is thereby removed. (The §13 heading retains "Task Adjudication" for S-8's remaining difficulty-grade and Skill-side-modification scope; the DEC-043 third-party adjudication ruling is unaffected.)
356: 
357: ---
358: 
359: # 14. Phase 7 — Extended Tests
360: 
361: Implement Extended Tests as repeated ordinary Tiwas tests. Each interval preserves Cost = Roll, Overflow → HP, Failure XP, failed Doubles, Advanced Skills, and Recovery.
362: 
363: Candidate progress models are Margin accumulation and Success count. Candidate failure models are stall, progress loss, and complication. Compare task completion time, resource depletion, failure frequency, growth, Overflow, and Advanced Skill generation. Progress must never become a second currency.
364: 
365: ---
366: 
367: # 15. Phase 8 — Cross-Cutting Architecture
368: 
369: Define Time (rounds, turns, actions, reactions, movement, intervals, ongoing timing); Conditions (application, stacking, duration, removal, interaction); Tags (weapon, armour, Effect, location, power, creature, setting); and Equipment (records, Traits, damage, carrying, encumbrance, repair/replacement).
370: 
371: Hazards use:
372: 
373: ```text
374: Trigger
375: → Existing Test
376: → Cost
377: → Outcome
378: → Existing Effect / Condition / Harm
379: ```
380: 
381: No subsystem-specific currency should be created.
382: 
383: **Note (v1.4.3):** per the S-2 non-attack deferral, the "Existing Effect / Condition / Harm" step above does not currently include Location Index output, even where the Trigger→Existing Test step produces a genuine Core Test roll. See Proposals/WIP §2.5A.
384: 
385: ---
386: 
387: # 16. Phase 9 — Rest and Healing
388: 
389: Implement the attrition loop after harm and death rules are sufficiently stable: Rest, resource recovery, wound recovery, healing time, ongoing conditions, and recovery from incapacitation. Evaluate against the requirement that Rest must not trivialize the resource identity.
390: 
391: ---
392: 
393: # 17. Phase 10 — Magic and Special Abilities
394: 
395: Implement a setting-facing power grammar around Advanced Skills. Verify Body-rooted and Mind-rooted powers, mixed-domain Advanced Skills, Overflow, failed Doubles, Conditions, Effects, and Extended Tests. Fixed spell lists may exist as setting content but must not be required by the Core.
396: 
397: ---
398: 
399: # 18. Phase 11 — NPC Compression
400: 
401: NPC construction should compress the same underlying mechanics rather than introduce a separate NPC engine. Evaluate encounter construction time, mathematical compatibility, resource behaviour, survivability, and challenge curves. NPC packages must still resolve through the same Universal Play architecture.
402: 
403: ---
404: 
405: # 19. Phase 12 — Setting Interface
406: 
407: A setting module may add content, permissions, creatures, equipment, powers, technology, magic, Tags, and Effects. It may not redefine d100, roll-under, 100-Fumble, Cost = Roll, Overflow → HP, Failure XP, Skill Roll Pool, Advanced Skill construction, or Core recovery.
408: 
409: > **Acceptance criterion:** A new setting can be implemented without modifying the Core Engine.
410: 
411: ---
412: 
413: # 20. Phase 13 — Full Integration Simulation
414: 
415: ## 20.1 Opposed exchanges
416: 
417: Test low versus high and equal Skill; Skill > 99; both succeed, one succeeds, and both fail; 100-Fumble; failed Doubles; and resource exhaustion.
418: 
419: ## 20.2 Combat
420: 
421: Test locations on/off and location tiers; armour; defense; Effects; Conditions; wounds; incapacitation; and death.
422: 
423: ## 20.3 Extended Tests
424: 
425: Compare progress and failure models, resource drain, Overflow, Failure XP, and Advanced Skill creation.
426: 
427: ## 20.4 Powers
428: 
429: Test Mind-rooted, Body-rooted, and mixed-domain powers; Overflow; failed Doubles; Conditions; and Effects.
430: 
431: ## 20.5 Non-combat
432: 
433: Test social contests, research, crafting, travel, hazards, stealth, and technical tasks.
434: 
435: **Note (v1.4.3):** hazard testing in this phase should confirm the absence of Location Index generation for non-attack cases, consistent with the S-2 non-attack deferral, unless that deferral has been explicitly reopened and superseded by then.
436: 
437: ---
438: 
439: # 21. Mandatory Regression Matrix
440: 
441: | Invariant | Required result |
442: |---|---|
443: | Cost = Roll | Resource expenditure equals natural roll |
444: | 100-Fumble | 100 always fails |
445: | 100 Double | 100 always qualifies as failed Double |
446: | Overflow → HP | Resource shortfall becomes HP damage |
447: | Failure XP | Failed tests generate XP |
448: | Failure-XP clamp | XP never becomes negative |
449: | Skill Roll Pool | Resolved within the same failed test |
450: | Cascading | Multiple increases possible where affordable |
451: | Cap ceiling | Skill Roll Pool cannot exceed Cap |
452: | General XP above Cap | Above-Cap Skill advancement remains possible |
453: | Advanced Skill trigger | Only qualifying failed Doubles trigger |
454: | Advanced Tier | Tier + 1 |
455: | Advanced Attribute | No duplicate attribute |
456: | Advanced Cap | Full formula recalculation |
457: | Resource lineage | Original Tier-1 domain controls resource |
458: | Live statistics | Attribute changes propagate immediately |
459: | Recovery | Always last |
460: | No parallel currencies | No competing primary resource/progression system |
461: 
462: ---
463: 
464: # 22. Acceptance Standard for a Complete Universal System
465: 
466: Tiwas should not be considered mechanically complete until every meaningful test uses the common Core transaction; opposed actions use the universal contest primitive; successful contests can create meaningful state change; harm supports both resource attrition and meaningful injury; location granularity is configurable; the completed death model preserves heroic resilience; combat and Extended Tests share coherent time architecture; Conditions and Tags are reusable; progression remains failure-driven; Extended Tests do not create a second currency; powers use the universal Skill architecture; NPCs use compressed versions of the same mechanics; settings can be added without modifying Core invariants; and the full regression suite passes.
467: 
468: ---
469: 
470: # 23. Project Governance
471: 
472: ## 23.1 Status transitions
473: 
474: ```text
475: Idea
476:  ↓
477: Proposal
478:  ↓
479: WIP
480:  ↓
481: Independent Review
482:  ↓
483: Simulation / Analysis
484:  ↓
485: Designer Ruling
486:  ↓
487: Accepted
488:  ↓
489: Locked / Canonical
490: ```
491: 
492: An item may return to WIP if evidence exposes a substantive problem.
493: 
494: ## 23.2 Evidence classes
495: 
496: Design documentation should distinguish:
497: 
498: - **Mechanical fact:** directly follows from existing locked rules.
499: - **Empirical finding:** supported by simulation, playtesting, or other explicit evidence.
500: - **Designer ruling:** a deliberate choice not mathematically forced by the system.
501: - **Recommendation:** a proposed preference not yet accepted.
502: - **Architectural constraint:** governs how systems interact rather than what a mechanic numerically does.
503: 
504: Evidence must be recorded with its scope and limitations. An empirical finding does not itself establish a designer ruling; an architectural constraint does not establish a numerical mechanic. Future documents should label these categories wherever confusion is likely.
505: 
506: ---
507: 
508: # 24. LLM Governance Rules
509: 
510: Future LLM sessions must:
511: 
512: 1. Treat Canonical Rules as authoritative.
513: 2. Treat Proposals/WIP as non-canonical.
514: 3. Treat Roadmap recommendations as implementation guidance.
515: 4. Never promote a proposal because it appears repeatedly in documentation.
516: 5. Never infer a numerical threshold from an example unless explicitly locked.
517: 6. Never silently resolve an open designer fork.
518: 7. Identify contradictions between current and historical documents.
519: 8. Prefer the current locked ruling over superseded source wording.
520: 9. Preserve the distinction between empirical evidence and designer judgement.
521: 10. State clearly when an answer depends on a proposal rather than a Canonical rule.
522: 11. Never create a parallel Core resolution engine merely to implement a subsystem.
523: 12. Never create a new primary resource or progression currency without explicit designer approval.
524: 13. Treat an interface prototype as non-canonical unless a formal ruling says otherwise.
525: 14. When a subsystem is locked, update the Canonical document and its changelog.
526: 15. When a proposal is superseded, retain its historical significance but clearly mark it Superseded.
527: 16. If new evidence materially challenges a locked rule, recommend reopening it rather than silently changing it.
528: 
529: ---
530: 
531: # 25. Documentation Maintenance Rule
532: 
533: The three consolidated documents should remain synchronized.
534: 
535: ## When a rule becomes locked
536: 
537: Update Canonical Rules, the Canonical Changelog, Proposal status, Roadmap status/dependencies, and regression requirements if applicable.
538: 
539: ## When a proposal changes
540: 
541: Update Proposals/WIP and the relevant Roadmap dependency or phase. Do not modify Canonical Rules.
542: 
543: ## When an implementation decision changes
544: 
545: Update the Roadmap and any relevant WIP note if it affects a design proposal. Do not modify Canonical Rules unless the actual game mechanic has changed through formal governance.
546: 
547: ---
548: 
549: # 26. Core Project Principle
550: 
551: The implementation target is not merely “complete combat.” The target is:
552: 
553: > **A universal state-resolution architecture in which combat, social conflict, hazards, crafting, research, travel, magic and other activities reuse the same Tiwas Core transaction.**
554: 
555: The central architectural rule is:
556: 
557: > **Every Universal Play Module must be an adapter around the locked Tiwas Core transaction, never a competing resolution, resource, progression, or recovery engine.**
558: 

(End of file - total 558 lines)
